tests: R14: one FINDING scan-found per found note scanFindings answers, keyed by capture and note, to each active member who may see the capture and to nobody else
R14 R7: a finding on a capture the viewer may not see is no item and is not counted; its subject is the capture's home (provenance.homeOf)

R14 R20: its summary and detail are queue.scan-found.summary and .detail: {document} the file's name, {engine} the engine, {names} the finding names, {meanings} each in findingKind's words, {date} the note's local day by date.daymonth; the file held, the safe view open, the release rule; it names no member and is no hint

R14 (T37): scanFindings is read with since the instant 90 days before the call, from the first page, following cursor while truncated, to at most 1,000 findings in pages of at most 200, as the viewer; facts name the bound and truncated
R14 (T37): every read starts again from since, never from a cursor kept between reads, so a finding older than the window is never read and never uses up the bound
R14 R1: a scanFindings or homeOf that throws or refuses contributes no item and is named in facts.failed; the read writes nothing
R15: one FINDING security-tool-off per event that switched a tool off, keyed by tool and instant, to each active administrator and to nobody else

R15 R20: its summary and detail are queue.security-tool-off.summary and .detail, {tool} the tool named: that it was switched off for not confirming its private mode, and that it stays off until an administrator tests it again; no file and no member
R15: raised once per event; it leaves when the tool is on again, and a later switch raises a fresh one
R15: securityToolEvents is followed by its cursor to at most 1,000 events under the administrator's own viewer, facts naming the bound and truncated
R15 R1: a read that refuses or throws contributes no item and is named in facts.failed; a member who is no administrator never asks; the read writes nothing

R14 (T37, N771, K2155): it leaves when its recipient disposes of it (the same key on every read while its hold is open) or when scanFindings answers held false, read in the same synchronous call; an item past the window is no longer answered: the window is the item's life (K2238)
R14 R20: {date} is the note's local day in the profile's zone, never the UTC day, and names its year when not in the current local year (date.daymonthyear); control: this year's names none
R26 (T51; N889; DEC-340) R14 and R15 write no day as ISO text: a note's day names its month and day by date.daymonth, and a tool's switch-off names no day at all

tests: R2 R9: a closed gate raises no item and counts none; once the gate is recorded at or under 20% each result is one FINDING interest-check-noticed, keyed by check and result
R2: the detail states the check's data-defined condition, its denominator and its cited derivation; the subject is the pattern, never the person; no judgment of a person
R2 R7: only to members of the project the check runs in who may see every input; a hidden input withholds the result from them; nobody else
R2: switched off for a project, a check raises nothing there; a group-wide check reaches each project of the member's that has not switched it off, one item homed under each
R2: raised once; it leaves when the result no longer holds (the read no longer answers it)
R8: an interest-check item offers only taking it up as a hunch or hypothesis; it is never a citation; the read stores nothing on a person or anywhere
R9: the gate is the only switch: no parameter of the read shows a gated check
R9: a second guard: a check whose answer does not say its gate is open raises nothing
R11: an interest-check item is marked "Hint · machine work" in its summary and detail, every sentence calls it a hint and none a signal; its label, kind and key unchanged

R2 R7 (D54; N822, K2408): an administrator at a hidden project's EXISTENCE is told nothing of its contents: no interest-check item for that project, which is never asked about for them; the control: joined, the same administrator receives it
R3 R9: no item before a rate is recorded, nor above 20%; at or under 20% one FINDING money-detector-noticed per result, keyed by detector and result, labelled the machine's
R3: detail, label and words as R2's: its denominator and derivation stated, the subject a pattern over facts, no judgment of anyone
R3 R7: only to members of that project who may see every input; one resting on a hidden project's fact reaches no outsider and is counted nowhere
R3: switched off for a project, a detector raises nothing there; a member of no project, a machine and no member receive none
R3: raised once per result (the same key on every read); it leaves when the result no longer holds
R8: a detector item offers only taking it up; never a citation; the read writes nothing
R9: a second guard: a result whose gate is absent or above 20% is never raised, whatever the provider answers
R11: a money-detector item is marked "Hint · machine work" in its summary and detail, every sentence calls it a hint and none a signal; its label, kind and key unchanged

R3 R7 (D54; N822, K2408): an administrator at a hidden project's EXISTENCE is told nothing of its contents: no detector item of that project and none asked of it; the control: joined, the same administrator receives it
R5: an adopted duty's occurrence the record shows overdue is one FINDING temporal-expectation-due, keyed by duty and occurrence, to the member who adopted it, `due` its local day; pending before
R5: never a violation: the detail says what the record shows, not a finding that a rule was broken, with its derivation; it says nothing of a breach

R5: an uncertain due date: between the candidates the item reads possibly overdue: undetermined, because …; after the latest, overdue, a fresh item keyed by its state; before the first, nothing (K1444 (i), K1676)
R5: it leaves when the occurrence is met or met late, or no longer overdue
R5: an occurrence of the group's own checkpoint is never an item (D234; action-plans R23)
R5: recipients: the adopting member, else the duty's project's owners, else the administrators; nobody else
R5: its age runs from the start of the due day in the due's own zone, never the UTC midnight (K1444 (iii), K1688)
R11: a duty's item, overdue or possibly overdue, is no hint: it carries no "Hint · machine work" mark and never calls itself a hint or a signal
R5 (T45): a duty stopped today raises no item for an occurrence due tomorrow; control: the same duty with no link (dutyWatchEndAt null) raises it; the duty stays held and its occurrence readable
R5 (T45): a duty kept until a day raises items up to that day and none after; the item already raised for the earlier occurrence is unchanged
R5 (T45): an undetermined due date is compared by its latest candidate: an end between the candidates tells nothing, an end on the latest tells the possibly-overdue item

R5 (T45) R21 R1: a following whose dutyWatchEndAt throws contributes no duty item and is named in facts.failed; an answer that is no {day, at} is read as no end (the duty still told); the read writes nothing

R18 an occurrence told while undetermined, then a stop whose end day falls before its latest candidate, still answers its item, the same key on every read until disposed; control: the same stop before the occurrence was told raises no item
R18 a told occurrence is exempt from the end of telling whole: once overdue after its latest candidate its overdue item is raised, as R5 raises it; control: an occurrence not told raises none
R18 a told occurrence still leaves when it is met, met late or no longer overdue, whatever the end

R21 a keep answered after an occurrence became possibly overdue leaves its item standing though its latest candidate falls after the kept day; control: the same occurrence becoming possibly overdue only after the answer raises none, though its first candidate falls before the kept day

outside.waitsOn: this module: code the checker accepts under the standard's settings
tests: R5: an adopted duty's occurrence the record shows overdue is one FINDING temporal-expectation-due, keyed by duty and occurrence, to the member who adopted it, `due` its local day; pending before
R5: never a violation: the detail says what the record shows, not a finding that a rule was broken, with its derivation; it says nothing of a breach

R5: an uncertain due date: between the candidates the item reads possibly overdue: undetermined, because …; after the latest, overdue, a fresh item keyed by its state; before the first, nothing (K1444 (i), K1676)
R5: it leaves when the occurrence is met or met late, or no longer overdue
R5: an occurrence of the group's own checkpoint is never an item (D234; action-plans R23)
R5: recipients: the adopting member, else the duty's project's owners, else the administrators; nobody else
R5: its age runs from the start of the due day in the due's own zone, never the UTC midnight (K1444 (iii), K1688)
R11: a duty's item, overdue or possibly overdue, is no hint: it carries no "Hint · machine work" mark and never calls itself a hint or a signal
R5 (T45): a duty stopped today raises no item for an occurrence due tomorrow; control: the same duty with no link (dutyWatchEndAt null) raises it; the duty stays held and its occurrence readable
R5 (T45): a duty kept until a day raises items up to that day and none after; the item already raised for the earlier occurrence is unchanged
R5 (T45): an undetermined due date is compared by its latest candidate: an end between the candidates tells nothing, an end on the latest tells the possibly-overdue item

R5 (T45) R21 R1: a following whose dutyWatchEndAt throws contributes no duty item and is named in facts.failed; an answer that is no {day, at} is read as no end (the duty still told); the read writes nothing

R18 an occurrence told while undetermined, then a stop whose end day falls before its latest candidate, still answers its item, the same key on every read until disposed; control: the same stop before the occurrence was told raises no item
R18 a told occurrence is exempt from the end of telling whole: once overdue after its latest candidate its overdue item is raised, as R5 raises it; control: an occurrence not told raises none
R18 a told occurrence still leaves when it is met, met late or no longer overdue, whatever the end

R21 a keep answered after an occurrence became possibly overdue leaves its item standing though its latest candidate falls after the kept day; control: the same occurrence becoming possibly overdue only after the answer raises none, though its first candidate falls before the kept day
R21 told means at or before the end's instant: an occurrence possibly overdue from the start of 2 October (UTC) is told by a stop answered at that instant, and not by one a second before

R20 R5: an overdue occurrence's summary and detail are queue.temporal-expectation-due.overdue.summary and .detail filled: {duty} and {what} the duty's act, {office} its obligor's registered name (K3144), {basis} its due's citation, {date} the due day by date.daymonth; an undetermined one's .undetermined.*, {reason} duties' reason.says (R22) and {from}, {to} its candidates
R20 R5: an occurrence due last year names its year (date.daymonthyear); control: one due this year does not

R22 an undetermined occurrence whose trigger is undated answers the words of trigger_undated in {reason}, naming no ISO date, zone id or ruling number, and its reason_code; control: its why text appears nowhere in the item's summary or detail
R22 each of duties' codes is answered as reason_code and its says fills {reason}; control: another code's words are not used
R22 an occurrence answering reason: null fills {reason} with nothing and draws no reason clause, and answers reason_code null; control: with a reason the clause is drawn
R22 over the real duties: a possibly overdue occurrence answers duties' reason code and says, in the item and its {reason}; an overdue one answers reason_code null
R26 (T51; N889; DEC-340) R5 writes no day as ISO text: its due day names its month and day, and an occurrence due last year names its year (control)
R14: one FINDING scan-found per found note scanFindings answers, keyed by capture and note, to each active member who may see the capture and to nobody else
R14 R7: a finding on a capture the viewer may not see is no item and is not counted; its subject is the capture's home (provenance.homeOf)

R14 R20: its summary and detail are queue.scan-found.summary and .detail: {document} the file's name, {engine} the engine, {names} the finding names, {meanings} each in findingKind's words, {date} the note's local day by date.daymonth; the file held, the safe view open, the release rule; it names no member and is no hint

R14 (T37): scanFindings is read with since the instant 90 days before the call, from the first page, following cursor while truncated, to at most 1,000 findings in pages of at most 200, as the viewer; facts name the bound and truncated
R14 (T37): every read starts again from since, never from a cursor kept between reads, so a finding older than the window is never read and never uses up the bound
R14 R1: a scanFindings or homeOf that throws or refuses contributes no item and is named in facts.failed; the read writes nothing
R15: one FINDING security-tool-off per event that switched a tool off, keyed by tool and instant, to each active administrator and to nobody else

R15 R20: its summary and detail are queue.security-tool-off.summary and .detail, {tool} the tool named: that it was switched off for not confirming its private mode, and that it stays off until an administrator tests it again; no file and no member
R15: raised once per event; it leaves when the tool is on again, and a later switch raises a fresh one
R15: securityToolEvents is followed by its cursor to at most 1,000 events under the administrator's own viewer, facts naming the bound and truncated
R15 R1: a read that refuses or throws contributes no item and is named in facts.failed; a member who is no administrator never asks; the read writes nothing

R14 (T37, N771, K2155): it leaves when its recipient disposes of it (the same key on every read while its hold is open) or when scanFindings answers held false, read in the same synchronous call; an item past the window is no longer answered: the window is the item's life (K2238)
R14 R20: {date} is the note's local day in the profile's zone, never the UTC day, and names its year when not in the current local year (date.daymonthyear); control: this year's names none
R26 (T51; N889; DEC-340) R14 and R15 write no day as ISO text: a note's day names its month and day by date.daymonth, and a tool's switch-off names no day at all
R13: one FINDING policy-changed-noticed per change with amendment_held false, keyed by watch and later capture, to the member who declared the policy and to nobody else

R13 R20: its summary and detail are queue.policy-changed-noticed.summary and .detail, the detail exactly DEC-145 (5)'s sentence as words.json holds it, {date} the local day of the earlier capture in the profile's zone by date.daymonth, {policy} the policy's cite
R13: it never says what the change means, never states a violation, is never a finding of the record, and is no hint (no R11 mark)
R13: it leaves when a later read answers the change with amendment_held true (a superseding version effective between the captures)
R13: a declarer no longer active, or a machine, sends it to the administrators instead
R13: only while the recipient may see the policy: a change policyChanges leaves out for that viewer is no item
R13: read for the changes whose later capture is no older than 90 days
R13: following cursor to at most 1,000 changes, facts naming the bound and truncated
R13: a following or standards that throws contributes no item and is named in facts.failed; the read writes nothing
R13 (T36): policyChanges is read with since, the instant 90 days before the call: a history of 1,200 changes older than the window is never read and never uses up the bound
R26 (T51; N889; DEC-340) R13 writes no day as ISO text: the earlier capture's day names its month and day, and its year in the next year
R12: while the level is Ordinary or Raised no item is raised; when it is High, one FINDING security-level-high to each active administrator and to nobody else
R12: the item is keyed by its episode's start, to the hour, and opens the security screen at that period, from the start to the instant derived
R12: an episode is an unbroken run: an earlier unusual hour before a quiet one is not part of it; a through starts it at its own hour; a through in the current hour starts it then
R12: raised once per episode: while it lasts, later reads answer the same key; once a read answers Raised or Ordinary it has ended, and a later episode raises a fresh one
R12: an episode longer than one securityMap read is read back hour by hour across reads; one reaching the days kept starts at the first hour kept
R12: its detail is one plain sentence: the level is High, since when, whether anything got through; counts only, naming no address, country, role, handle or member
R12 R20: the security-level item keeps its plain sentence: words.json holds no key for it and it answers none (control: R15's item, beside it, answers its keys)
R12: a securityLevel or securityMap that throws or does not answer contributes no item and is named in facts.failed, never read as Ordinary; the read writes nothing

R25 (T51; DEC-299, DEC-333, DEC-335) the security item's instant is a plain date and time in the team's zone: an episode starting 2026-10-16T16:00:00Z for a team in the Pacific zone reads 9:00 AM; with no zone the UTC reading and UTC; control: id and screen.from stay ISO, and a second read in the episode keeps the id
R4: one FINDING standing-answer per run that found something new, keyed by question and run, to the question's author and to nobody else
R4: told once: raised once per run and never repeated (a later read answers the same run's item, never a second); a run with nothing new raises none
R4: the detail names the new finds and the answer as answers holds it, or what held the AI half back, in plain words
R4: answers' pages are followed to their bound, and a cut is stated in facts
R11: a standing answer is no hint: it carries no "Hint · machine work" mark and never calls itself a hint or a signal
R4 (DEC-149, T34-87): what held the AI half back calls the group's Civicsmith "your group's Civicsmith", never this copy, plane, instance or server
R6: a wait due on the local day is one OBLIGATION inquiry-recheck-due, keyed by inquiry and date, to the member who set it and to nobody else; waiting before its local day

R6 R20: it names what is awaited, from whom and by when (DEC-98), in queue.inquiry-recheck-due.summary's and .detail's words: {question} the inquiry's title, {what} the wait's text, {who} its description (its own leading "from" left to the sentence), {date} its day by date.daymonth
R6: raised once; it leaves when its setter records a look, sets a new date or removes the wait, or the inquiry concludes
R6: an inquiry the viewer may not see raises nothing
R6: its age runs from the start of the wait's local day in inquiry's zone, never the UTC midnight (K1444 (iii), K1688): west of UTC, at the day boundary
R6: with no zone in inquiry's answer, the age is undetermined, never computed on the UTC day
R11: a dated wait's to-do is no hint: it carries no "Hint · machine work" mark and never calls itself a hint or a signal
R20 R6: a wait due on a day of last year names its year (date.daymonthyear); several waits on one day are one item naming each; control: a wait with no description names its text as from whom
R26 (T51; N889; DEC-340) R6 writes no day as ISO text: a wait's day names its month and day and its year when it is last year's

R16 the overall limit reads ai.queue.limitreached.overall and the per-member limit ai.queue.limitreached.member, each by key and naming no member; each scope's sentence differs from the other two (K874)

R16 a month's limit on a member's own account: {account} from ai.account.own, {period} ai.period.month, {when} after "until" from ai.until.month with the next period's month from date.month.*; the group's limit from ai.account.group, to its administrators only

R16 a limit's {date} is the profile's local day reached_at falls on, never the UTC day; every use of ai-use's nine reads its ai.use.<use>.inline (DEC-191 (2)), a scope with no such key the overall limit's sentence (J1 (3)); an entry whose period or day cannot be read is no item

R16 one Ask item per entry of ai-use.exploreAsksPending, keyed by its own key, in ai.queue.exploreask's words: {scope} the project's name, or ai.scope.group / ai.scope.own; {account} from ai.account.<kind>.inline; offering act.exploreapprove; to the account's owners only; gone once approved

R16 one Noticed project-account-suspended item per entry of ai-accounts.projectAccountsSuspended (T48: R16 reads it there, never from credentials), keyed by its own key, in ai.queue.suspended's words naming the project and no member; to the project's owner alone, and none while the sign-in serves
R16 R1 a read that does not answer is its provider's failure, named in facts.failed, never read as no item; the bound and truncated stated

R16 (T44) {date}: reached_at on 7 October local reads "7 October" (date.daymonth, no leading zero); an instant that is the 6th locally and the 7th in UTC reads "6 October" (control); a day in another local year reads "{day} {month} {year}" (date.daymonthyear; control: this year's has no year); {when} reads "1 November" after "until"
R5: an adopted duty's occurrence the record shows overdue is one FINDING temporal-expectation-due, keyed by duty and occurrence, to the member who adopted it, `due` its local day; pending before
R5: never a violation: the detail says what the record shows, not a finding that a rule was broken, with its derivation; it says nothing of a breach

R5: an uncertain due date: between the candidates the item reads possibly overdue: undetermined, because …; after the latest, overdue, a fresh item keyed by its state; before the first, nothing (K1444 (i), K1676)
R5: it leaves when the occurrence is met or met late, or no longer overdue
R5: an occurrence of the group's own checkpoint is never an item (D234; action-plans R23)
R5: recipients: the adopting member, else the duty's project's owners, else the administrators; nobody else
R5: its age runs from the start of the due day in the due's own zone, never the UTC midnight (K1444 (iii), K1688)
R11: a duty's item, overdue or possibly overdue, is no hint: it carries no "Hint · machine work" mark and never calls itself a hint or a signal
R5 (T45): a duty stopped today raises no item for an occurrence due tomorrow; control: the same duty with no link (dutyWatchEndAt null) raises it; the duty stays held and its occurrence readable
R5 (T45): a duty kept until a day raises items up to that day and none after; the item already raised for the earlier occurrence is unchanged
R5 (T45): an undetermined due date is compared by its latest candidate: an end between the candidates tells nothing, an end on the latest tells the possibly-overdue item

R5 (T45) R21 R1: a following whose dutyWatchEndAt throws contributes no duty item and is named in facts.failed; an answer that is no {day, at} is read as no end (the duty still told); the read writes nothing

R18 an occurrence told while undetermined, then a stop whose end day falls before its latest candidate, still answers its item, the same key on every read until disposed; control: the same stop before the occurrence was told raises no item
R18 a told occurrence is exempt from the end of telling whole: once overdue after its latest candidate its overdue item is raised, as R5 raises it; control: an occurrence not told raises none
R18 a told occurrence still leaves when it is met, met late or no longer overdue, whatever the end

R21 a keep answered after an occurrence became possibly overdue leaves its item standing though its latest candidate falls after the kept day; control: the same occurrence becoming possibly overdue only after the answer raises none, though its first candidate falls before the kept day
R21 told means at or before the end's instant: an occurrence possibly overdue from the start of 2 October (UTC) is told by a stop answered at that instant, and not by one a second before

R20 R5: an overdue occurrence's summary and detail are queue.temporal-expectation-due.overdue.summary and .detail filled: {duty} and {what} the duty's act, {office} its obligor's registered name (K3144), {basis} its due's citation, {date} the due day by date.daymonth; an undetermined one's .undetermined.*, {reason} duties' reason.says (R22) and {from}, {to} its candidates
R20 R5: an occurrence due last year names its year (date.daymonthyear); control: one due this year does not

R22 an undetermined occurrence whose trigger is undated answers the words of trigger_undated in {reason}, naming no ISO date, zone id or ruling number, and its reason_code; control: its why text appears nowhere in the item's summary or detail
R22 each of duties' codes is answered as reason_code and its says fills {reason}; control: another code's words are not used
R22 an occurrence answering reason: null fills {reason} with nothing and draws no reason clause, and answers reason_code null; control: with a reason the clause is drawn
R22 over the real duties: a possibly overdue occurrence answers duties' reason code and says, in the item and its {reason}; an overdue one answers reason_code null
R26 (T51; N889; DEC-340) R5 writes no day as ISO text: its due day names its month and day, and an occurrence due last year names its year (control)
R14: one FINDING scan-found per found note scanFindings answers, keyed by capture and note, to each active member who may see the capture and to nobody else
R14 R7: a finding on a capture the viewer may not see is no item and is not counted; its subject is the capture's home (provenance.homeOf)

R14 R20: its summary and detail are queue.scan-found.summary and .detail: {document} the file's name, {engine} the engine, {names} the finding names, {meanings} each in findingKind's words, {date} the note's local day by date.daymonth; the file held, the safe view open, the release rule; it names no member and is no hint

R14 (T37): scanFindings is read with since the instant 90 days before the call, from the first page, following cursor while truncated, to at most 1,000 findings in pages of at most 200, as the viewer; facts name the bound and truncated
R14 (T37): every read starts again from since, never from a cursor kept between reads, so a finding older than the window is never read and never uses up the bound
R14 R1: a scanFindings or homeOf that throws or refuses contributes no item and is named in facts.failed; the read writes nothing
R15: one FINDING security-tool-off per event that switched a tool off, keyed by tool and instant, to each active administrator and to nobody else

R15 R20: its summary and detail are queue.security-tool-off.summary and .detail, {tool} the tool named: that it was switched off for not confirming its private mode, and that it stays off until an administrator tests it again; no file and no member
R15: raised once per event; it leaves when the tool is on again, and a later switch raises a fresh one
R15: securityToolEvents is followed by its cursor to at most 1,000 events under the administrator's own viewer, facts naming the bound and truncated
R15 R1: a read that refuses or throws contributes no item and is named in facts.failed; a member who is no administrator never asks; the read writes nothing

R14 (T37, N771, K2155): it leaves when its recipient disposes of it (the same key on every read while its hold is open) or when scanFindings answers held false, read in the same synchronous call; an item past the window is no longer answered: the window is the item's life (K2238)
R14 R20: {date} is the note's local day in the profile's zone, never the UTC day, and names its year when not in the current local year (date.daymonthyear); control: this year's names none
R26 (T51; N889; DEC-340) R14 and R15 write no day as ISO text: a note's day names its month and day by date.daymonth, and a tool's switch-off names no day at all
R17 step-later-found: one FINDING per entry steps.laterFound answers, keyed by its key, to each it answers and to nobody else; told once
R17 step-date-due and step-reminder: OBLIGATIONs from steps.stepsDue, keyed by its key, to the member who set the date or asked for the reminder and to nobody else
R17 (T45) a step whose byWhen an action's clock entry holds (steps R29) draws no step-date-due; control: with no holder registered, the same step raises one; her own reminder on it stays

R17 step-cost-shared and step-cost-message: FINDINGs from steps.costShares and costMessages, to the sharing projects' owners and to whom a message was relayed; nothing when a sharing project is hidden
R17 milestone-overdue (FINDING, to each joined participant) and milestone-reminder (OBLIGATION, to the member who asked), from investigation.milestonesOverdue, keyed by its key
R17 project-quiet: one FINDING per quiet spell from investigation.quietPrompts, keyed by its key, to the joined participants; nothing more once a member took a door

R17 question-find: one FINDING per find question-explorer.findsFor answers, keyed by its key, marked "Hint · machine work"; the label ai.label.explored with {owner} filled from ai-use R6's enabled_by only for that account's owners, ai.label.explored.member for every other viewer (D64; DEC-189 (7))
R17 review-comment-left-out: one FINDING per entry review.reviewCommentsLeftOut answers, its key used whole, to the member reviewer and to nobody else; none when every comment was carried
R17 R1 each source's bound and truncated stated; a source that throws or refuses contributes no item and is named in facts.failed; the read writes nothing
R17 step-later-found's {date} is the look's own local day when steps answers it (looked_at), else the entry's (J1 (4)); {what} the step's work, else its id

R17 (T44) each {date}: step-later-found, step-date-due and milestone-overdue fill {date} as R16's: the local day by date.daymonth, by date.daymonthyear outside the current local year (control: inside it, no year); a look on the 6th locally and the 7th in UTC reads the 6th (control: in UTC, the 7th)

R19 a member with 1,001 open dated steps has facts.step_due truncated (stepsDue's own bound reached), the items drawn unchanged; control: with 1,000, not; and 1,001 reminders due likewise (control: 1,000)
R13: one FINDING policy-changed-noticed per change with amendment_held false, keyed by watch and later capture, to the member who declared the policy and to nobody else

R13 R20: its summary and detail are queue.policy-changed-noticed.summary and .detail, the detail exactly DEC-145 (5)'s sentence as words.json holds it, {date} the local day of the earlier capture in the profile's zone by date.daymonth, {policy} the policy's cite
R13: it never says what the change means, never states a violation, is never a finding of the record, and is no hint (no R11 mark)
R13: it leaves when a later read answers the change with amendment_held true (a superseding version effective between the captures)
R13: a declarer no longer active, or a machine, sends it to the administrators instead
R13: only while the recipient may see the policy: a change policyChanges leaves out for that viewer is no item
R13: read for the changes whose later capture is no older than 90 days
R13: following cursor to at most 1,000 changes, facts naming the bound and truncated
R13: a following or standards that throws contributes no item and is named in facts.failed; the read writes nothing
R13 (T36): policyChanges is read with since, the instant 90 days before the call: a history of 1,200 changes older than the window is never read and never uses up the bound
R26 (T51; N889; DEC-340) R13 writes no day as ISO text: the earlier capture's day names its month and day, and its year in the next year
R6: a wait due on the local day is one OBLIGATION inquiry-recheck-due, keyed by inquiry and date, to the member who set it and to nobody else; waiting before its local day

R6 R20: it names what is awaited, from whom and by when (DEC-98), in queue.inquiry-recheck-due.summary's and .detail's words: {question} the inquiry's title, {what} the wait's text, {who} its description (its own leading "from" left to the sentence), {date} its day by date.daymonth
R6: raised once; it leaves when its setter records a look, sets a new date or removes the wait, or the inquiry concludes
R6: an inquiry the viewer may not see raises nothing
R6: its age runs from the start of the wait's local day in inquiry's zone, never the UTC midnight (K1444 (iii), K1688): west of UTC, at the day boundary
R6: with no zone in inquiry's answer, the age is undetermined, never computed on the UTC day
R11: a dated wait's to-do is no hint: it carries no "Hint · machine work" mark and never calls itself a hint or a signal
R20 R6: a wait due on a day of last year names its year (date.daymonthyear); several waits on one day are one item naming each; control: a wait with no description names its text as from whom
R26 (T51; N889; DEC-340) R6 writes no day as ISO text: a wait's day names its month and day and its year when it is last year's
